companies.name: Impossible Metals
companies.oneLiner: Underwater robots that collect battery metals from the ocean floor.
companies.description: Impossible Metals develops underwater robotic vehicles that selectively harvest polymetallic nodules containing critical battery metals from the deep seafloor. Its approach uses precision robotics to minimize environmental disruption compared to traditional seafloor mining. The company targets the growing demand for nickel, cobalt, and manganese for EV and grid batteries.
companies.whyListed: Deep-sea critical mineral extraction is a compelling alternative supply chain to land-based mining; Impossible Metals sits at the intersection of robotics and critical minerals, two high-conviction hard-tech themes.

companies.name: Albedo
companies.oneLiner: Full-stack VLEO satellite missions for ultra-high-resolution imaging.
companies.description: Albedo is building satellites that operate in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) to capture imagery at significantly higher resolution than traditional commercial satellites. Operating closer to Earth allows smaller, cheaper satellites to achieve resolutions previously only available to government reconnaissance assets. The company targets defense, intelligence, and commercial geospatial markets.
companies.whyListed: Sub-30cm commercial satellite imagery is a strategic capability gap; Albedo's VLEO approach is a technically differentiated bet on democratizing reconnaissance-grade imagery.

companies.name: Inversion Space
companies.oneLiner: Space-based cargo return vehicles for rapid Earth delivery.
companies.description: Inversion Space is building reusable re-entry vehicles that can store cargo in orbit and rapidly deliver it to any point on Earth on demand. The concept turns space into a logistics layer enabling hours-long point-to-point delivery of high-value payloads. The company targets both commercial and defense logistics markets.
companies.whyListed: On-demand global cargo delivery from orbit addresses a unique defense and commercial logistics need; Inversion Space is pioneering a new category of orbital infrastructure with strong DoD relevance.

companies.name: TransAstra Corporation
companies.oneLiner: Orbital logistics and asteroid resource utilization infrastructure.
companies.description: TransAstra is developing orbital logistics systems including space tugs and asteroid mining technology to enable large-scale space industry. Their Worker Bee space tug uses solar thermal propulsion for efficient in-space transportation. The company targets the emerging cislunar economy and in-space propellant market.
companies.whyListed: In-space logistics and resource utilization are foundational to any sustained orbital or cislunar economy; TransAstra's solar thermal approach is technically differentiated with long-term strategic value.

companies.name: HEO Robotics
companies.oneLiner: Visual monitoring of space objects for governments and defense.
companies.description: HEO Robotics provides space domain awareness by hosting imaging payloads on third-party satellites to photograph other objects in orbit. This hosted payload model allows rapid, low-cost deployment of monitoring capability without dedicated spacecraft. Customers include government and defense agencies needing to track satellites and debris.
companies.whyListed: Space domain awareness is a top DoD priority as orbital congestion and adversarial satellite activity increase; HEO's hosted payload model is a capital-efficient approach to a high-value defense market.

companies.name: AstroForge
companies.oneLiner: Asteroid mining for platinum-group and critical metals.
companies.description: AstroForge is developing technology to mine and refine platinum-group metals from asteroids in space. The company plans to process asteroid material in orbit and return refined metals to Earth, targeting the high-value platinum-group metals market. companies.description: OS3 deploys US-built humanoid robots and trains video action models to enable general-purpose robotic manipulation and locomotion. The company is part of YC's Summer 2026 batch, positioning it at the intersection of domestic hardware manufacturing and foundation model development for robotics. Its focus on US-built hardware addresses supply chain and national security concerns.
companies.whyListed: Combining domestic humanoid hardware manufacturing with proprietary video action model training addresses both geopolitical hardware risk and the data bottleneck in general-purpose robotics.

companies.name: Dreamscale Labs
companies.oneLiner: Cloud compute infrastructure for running robot brain models.
companies.description: Dreamscale Labs provides cloud-based compute infrastructure specifically designed for running robot foundation models and inference workloads. The company enables robot operators to offload computationally intensive AI inference from edge hardware to the cloud, reducing onboard compute requirements. This is a critical infrastructure layer as humanoid and industrial robots scale.
companies.whyListed: Cloud robotics inference infrastructure is a capital-efficient wedge into the massive robot-as-a-service stack; offloading robot brain computation enables faster iteration and lower hardware BOM costs at scale.

companies.name: Maven Robotics
companies.oneLiner: Robot deployment platform with active enterprise deployments at scale
companies.description: Maven Robotics provides end-to-end robot deployment solutions for enterprise customers, emerging from stealth with $100M Series A and active production deployments already in place. The company targets the gap between robot manufacturers and end-users by handling integration, deployment, and ongoing operations. Their approach competes directly with in-house robot deployment programs at large enterprises.
companies.whyListed: A $100M Series A with active deployments signals Maven has cracked early commercialization in industrial robotics deployment — a critical bottleneck for the sector's growth.

companies.name: Poseidon Aerospace
companies.oneLiner: Large cargo drones and autonomous maritime logistics platforms for defense
companies.description: Poseidon Aerospace is developing Egret, a large-format cargo drone, alongside a maritime autonomous platform, targeting contested logistics for defense customers. The Bay Area startup raised $60M to fund flight testing, production scaling, and acceleration of its seafaring system. Their focus on large-payload autonomous logistics fills a critical gap in military supply chain resilience.
companies.whyListed: Contested logistics is an urgent DoD priority; large cargo drones with maritime variants address a dual-domain gap that smaller drone startups cannot fill.

companies.name: Covenant
companies.oneLiner: Deep precision strike systems for long-range lethal effects
companies.description: Covenant emerged from stealth with $250M in funding from a16z, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, 8VC, Aleph, and Lightspeed to develop deep precision strike capabilities. The company is focused on long-range strike munitions or systems designed for high-priority, contested target sets. The all-star investor syndicate suggests strong conviction in Covenant's technology differentiation and defense contract pipeline.
companies.whyListed: Deep precision strike is a top Pentagon investment priority; a $250M stealth raise backed by every major defense-tech investor signals Covenant has serious hardware and a credible path to large DoD programs.

companies.name: Bulwark Dynamics
companies.oneLiner: Unmanned surface vessels for contested maritime logistics
companies.description: Bulwark Dynamics builds unmanned surface vessels (USVs) purpose-built for contested logistics, enabling resupply and maritime operations in denied or high-threat environments. The California-based startup raised $6.8M in seed funding to ramp development and early deployments. Their laser focus on the logistics mission set differentiates them from ISR-first maritime drone competitors.
companies.whyListed: Maritime autonomy for contested logistics is an urgent and underfunded DoD need; Bulwark's mission-specific USV approach targets a clear capability gap with a lean seed-stage entry point.

companies.name: Ground A
companies.oneLiner: Laser-based counter-UAS systems for drone defense
companies.description: Ground A is a German directed-energy startup developing laser-based counter-UAS (cUAS) systems, raising €9.1M just eight months after founding. Their flagship system targets the growing threat of low-cost drone swarms with a high-capacity, low-cost-per-shot directed-energy solution. The European defense market and NATO partners represent their primary near-term customer base.
companies.whyListed: Directed-energy cUAS is a top-priority capability gap across NATO; a European laser startup raising pre-seed at this speed signals strong government customer pull and technical credibility.

companies.name: Iron Grid
companies.oneLiner: Foundation models for physical systems and industrial automation
companies.description: Iron Grid is building foundation models specifically designed for physical systems, targeting industrial automation and robotics applications. Their approach adapts the large-model paradigm from software AI to the sensing, control, and actuation challenges of real-world physical environments. The YC-backed company is positioned at the intersection of AI and hard-tech manufacturing.
companies.whyListed: Foundation models for physical systems are a prerequisite for general industrial automation; a YC-backed team attacking this layer could become infrastructure for the broader robotics stack.

companies.name: Rune Technologies
companies.stage: $4.1M Army AAL contract with 1st Cavalry Division
companies.oneLiner: Defense logistics OS for Army unit operations and supply chains.
companies.description: Rune Technologies builds TyrOS, a logistics operating system for military units. The company just secured a $4.1M Army contract through the Army Applications Laboratory to expand TyrOS deployment across the 1st Cavalry Division. It targets the unglamorous but critical software layer that keeps military formations supplied and coordinated.
companies.whyListed: Defense logistics software with proven Army adoption and contract revenue is a durable wedge into military operations tech — an underserved niche in the defense startup ecosystem.

companies.name: Inflection Space Systems
companies.oneLiner: Hyperscale manufacturing infrastructure for the space economy.
companies.description: Inflection Space Systems is building manufacturing infrastructure designed to scale production for the space industry. The company is part of YC's Fall 2026 batch, targeting the emerging need for high-throughput, low-cost space hardware fabrication. Few details are public, but the thesis mirrors terrestrial contract manufacturing applied to orbital hardware.
companies.whyListed: Space manufacturing capacity is a hard bottleneck on the entire new space economy; a company purpose-built to hyperscale that process addresses a critical infrastructure gap.

companies.name: Aviern
companies.oneLiner: Unmanned fixed-wing aircraft for geospatial intelligence collection.
companies.description: Aviern builds unmanned airplanes optimized for geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) missions. The company is in YC's Fall 2026 batch, targeting the growing demand for persistent ISR from autonomous fixed-wing platforms. Its focus on GEOINT aligns with both defense and intelligence community procurement priorities.
companies.whyListed: Autonomous ISR platforms are among the fastest-growing segments of the defense drone market, and fixed-wing endurance aircraft fill a persistent gap between satellites and short-range quadcopters.

companies.name: Micora
companies.oneLiner: Rapidly deployable modular microgrids built anywhere in days.
companies.description: Micora packages microgrid infrastructure into deployable units that can be installed anywhere within days. The company targets the growing demand for resilient, distributed power at the edge — from military forward operating bases to remote industrial sites. Its 'microgrid in a box' approach compresses the typical months-long deployment timeline.
companies.whyListed: Rapidly deployable distributed energy is both a defense logistics enabler and a critical infrastructure resilience play — two converging tailwinds that make this a compelling hard-tech bet.

companies.name: Darwin
companies.oneLiner: Humanoid robots for real-world physical labor tasks.
companies.description: Darwin is building humanoid robots, competing in the rapidly expanding market for general-purpose bipedal machines. The company came through YC's Fall 2025 batch. Details on its hardware architecture and target deployment verticals are limited, but it is positioned in the foundational humanoid platform race.
companies.whyListed: Humanoid robots represent one of the highest-conviction hardware bets of the decade; early-stage entrants with differentiated approaches to locomotion or manipulation are worth tracking closely.

companies.name: Deploy
companies.oneLiner: Generalist robot deployment company for real-world environments.
companies.description: Deploy is building the infrastructure and operations layer to deploy generalist robots at scale across real-world environments. The company is in YC's Fall 2026 batch and focuses on the deployment side of the robotics stack — the integration, management, and scaling challenge that often outlasts the hardware problem. Its generalist positioning suggests a horizontal play across industrial and commercial verticals.
companies.whyListed: The bottleneck in robotics is increasingly deployment and fleet management, not hardware; a company that cracks generalist robot deployment at scale could become critical infrastructure for the autonomy economy.

companies.name: Magnet
companies.oneLiner: Maritime autonomy company building medium unmanned surface vessels.
companies.description: Magnet is a stealth American maritime autonomy company that has partnered with Hanwha Defense USA to produce Medium Unmanned Surface Vessels (MUSVs). The partnership is set to kick off production in fall 2026, combining Hanwha's shipbuilding scale with Magnet's autonomy technology. The company operates with a low public profile despite the significance of the teaming arrangement.
companies.whyListed: Autonomous surface vessels are a high-priority DoD investment area; this partnership with a major defense prime signals serious production intent and near-term revenue.

companies.name: Viraj Aero
companies.oneLiner: Next-generation turbine engines for aircraft and data centers.
companies.description: Viraj Aero is developing advanced engine technology targeting both aviation and data center power generation markets. The company aims to bring high-efficiency turbine solutions to two of the fastest-growing power demand sectors. As a YC Fall 2026 company, they are in the earliest stages of development.
companies.whyListed: Dual-market engine technology addressing the acute data center power crisis and aviation decarbonization represents a high-leverage hard-tech bet at the intersection of energy and aerospace.

companies.name: Invertix
companies.oneLiner: AI that autonomously operates and optimizes critical energy infrastructure.
companies.description: Invertix is building AI-driven autonomy systems for critical energy infrastructure operations, positioning itself as 'energy superintelligence.' The platform is designed to make real-time operational decisions across grid and energy systems. As a YC Fall 2026 company, they are at the earliest stage.
companies.whyListed: Grid automation and AI-driven operations of critical infrastructure is a growing national security and energy transition priority, making this a compelling early-stage hard-tech watch.
